title: Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
intro: The young Ibrahim (AS) found his Lord by thinking about creation – and his family helped build Makkah and the Ka‘bah.

learn.html: The story of Ibrahim (AS), one of Allah’s chosen messengers, holds a lesson for all peoples until the end of this world. Ibrahim (AS) came from a people who worshipped statues, yet even as a child he knew that statues cannot be worshipped and should not be bowed to. Instead he thought about his Lord by looking at the nature around him.

learn.text: The star, the moon and the sun

learn.html: One evening, while he was a boy, he went outside and admired a star shining brightly in the sky. Amazed by its beauty, he called out that it was his Lord – but when the star disappeared, he said he does not love things that disappear. Then he saw the full moon and said: “This is my Lord!” When the moon also set, he said: “If my Lord does not guide me, I will be among those who are lost.”

Thinking like this, he hardly noticed the morning come, with the sun rising in full brightness. Ibrahim said: “This is my Lord – it is the biggest!” But when the sun set too, he said: “I have nothing to do with what you make equal to Him. I turn my face, as a true believer, to the One who created the heavens and the earth.”
Ibrahim (AS) wondered at his father Azar and said to him: “Do you take idols as gods? You and your people are clearly lost.”

One day, while his people were away at a celebration, Ibrahim (AS) went to the statues and broke them all – except the biggest one. When the people came back and saw their idols smashed, they remembered that he had spoken badly about them, so they guessed who had destroyed their “gods”. They asked him: “Ibrahim, did you do this?” He pointed at the biggest statue and told them to ask it. They said: “It can’t speak.” “Then why do you worship them?” said Ibrahim. “Yes, I defeated them – and you see, they couldn’t help themselves, so how can they help you?”

learn.title: 🔥 Cool and safe
learn.html: They decided to punish him by throwing him into a fire. They lit a huge fire and threw him in. But Allah (SWT) commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim, so he was not burned.

When he grew up, Ibrahim (AS) married Sarah, the most beautiful woman of her time. Allah gave them happiness and wealth, but they had no children, so Ibrahim kept asking Allah to give him a child – and that dua was answered later.

When Allah commanded him to move, Ibrahim, his wife Sarah, Lut (AS) and the believers left Mesopotamia and set off for the blessed land of Al-Quds (Jerusalem). They lived as nomads, moving with their flocks from pasture to pasture, and the road took them to Egypt. Egypt was ruled by an unjust king who wanted to take Sarah for himself. Ibrahim could not refuse the king, but he could make dua to Allah to save them. Whenever the king reached out his hand towards Sarah, Allah made his hand go stiff. He begged Sarah to pray for his hand to be healed, promising he would not do it again; she prayed and his hand was healed. After a few tries the king became afraid, gave Sarah a servant named Hajar as a gift, and sent Ibrahim and Sarah away.

Sarah allowed Ibrahim to marry Hajar, and Hajar gave birth to a son, Isma‘il. By Allah’s command, Ibrahim took Hajar and Isma‘il to the area of today’s Makkah. They stopped in a place with no water and no farmland. Trusting in Allah, Ibrahim (AS) left them there with a little water and dates.

learn.title: 💧 Zamzam
learn.html: When the water ran out, Hajar ran again and again between the hills of Safa and Marwah, looking for water for herself and her baby. When she had lost all hope and stopped beside Isma‘il, she saw water gushing out from under his feet. Afraid that the strong stream would flow away, she made a wall of sand around it and called out: “Zam-zam!” (“Stop! Stop!”). From then on, people began to settle in the valley of Makkah.

learn.text: The great test and the Ka‘bah

learn.html: When Isma‘il was old enough to help his father, Allah (SWT) commanded Ibrahim in a dream to sacrifice his son. This was really Ibrahim’s own promise from when he had asked Allah for a son. When the dream came a third time, Ibrahim told his son about his promise and Allah’s command. Isma‘il humbly agreed to be sacrificed and told his father to do what he had promised Allah and what he was commanded in the dream: “I will truly be patient,” said Isma‘il.

When Ibrahim had laid him face down and was firmly determined to sacrifice him, Allah (SWT) made them both happy with a great sacrifice – an animal brought by the angel Jibril. This is the origin of the Qurbani we still give at Eid al-Adha.

learn.title: 🕋 Building the Ka‘bah
learn.html: Later Allah commanded Ibrahim (AS) to build the Ka‘bah. His son Isma‘il helped him. In the eastern corner of the Ka‘bah, Ibrahim set a very special stone, known as Al-Hajar al-Aswad – the Black Stone.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: The stories of Allah’s messengers are very important for us, because we can learn from the examples of them and their peoples.

practice.title: Questions and talk
prompts: ❓ Who was Ibrahim (AS), and did he follow his people’s religion?
🌟 Retell what happened in Ibrahim’s youth as a result of thinking about his Lord.
👨‍👩‍👦 What were the names of Ibrahim’s wives, and which child did he have with each?
🕋 What did Ibrahim leave behind that we still recognise today? Which practices from his time do we still keep (Qurbani, Hajj, Sa‘i between Safa and Marwah, Zamzam)?

🗣️ Talk with your muallim: Al-Baqarah 2:258 – a ruler argued with Ibrahim about his Lord. Ibrahim said: “My Lord is the One who gives life and death.” The ruler said: “I give life and death.” Ibrahim said: “Allah brings the sun up from the east – so bring it up from the west!” And the disbeliever was left speechless. What does this teach us?
